column.text: Hyperliquid whales are leaning hard against the crowd, and that divergence is the signal to trade. Whale desks are net short BTC at -$649M, ETH at -$383M and SOL at -$101M, while retail sits at a long-to-short ratio of 2.77. Price is being propped up by short liquidations, not organic buying, and the tape is still down-trending. That is a long squeeze setup, and the regime favors continuation shorts. Flows confirm the bias. Friday 6 Nov saw ETF outflows of -$411.9M for BTC, -$93.2M for ETH and -$25.1M for SOL. Over the 7-day window, net redemptions reached -$1908.0M for BTC, -$626.6M for ETH and -$64.7M for SOL. Institutions are not paying up here. Supply is moving the wrong way too. Glassnode reports that most recent altcoin buyers exited at a loss by the end of October. Meanwhile, wallet 2MdNva collected 299,838 SOL from multiple token creators and sent it to exchanges, with about $26M in SOL dumped. MARA posted a profit but sold 13,597 BTC to pay off loans, so miners are raising cash. Macro adds pressure. The market prices an 80% probability of a Fed rate hike in December, dollar liquidity is contracting, and Fear & Greed sits at 32. Longs need a real mechanism: deeply negative funding, a capitulation reading, or a failed breakdown. Until one appears, treat rallies into resistance as better-odds shorts. Expect the squeeze to unwind into the December Fed decision, and sell strength until the whales prove wrong.
